examples.solution_text:
Multiply each term inside the bracket by $\sqrt{10}$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\sqrt{10}(\sqrt{5}+\sqrt{2})\\&=\sqrt{50}+\sqrt{20}\\&=5\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

Distribute the negative coefficient to both terms.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-3\sqrt{2}(2\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2})\\&=-6\sqrt{12}+3\sqrt{4}\\&=-12\sqrt{3}+6\end{aligned}$

Multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(\sqrt{10}-2)(\sqrt{10}+3)\\&=10+3\sqrt{10}-2\sqrt{10}-6\\&=4+\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(3-2\sqrt{5})^{2}\\&=9-12\sqrt{5}+4\times5\\&=29-12\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$
Match the rational term and the coefficient of $\sqrt{5}$: $a=29$ and $b=-12$.

Expand both squares, then subtract every term in the second expansion.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{2})^{2}-(\sqrt{10}-\sqrt{2})^{2}\\&=(10+2\sqrt{20}+2)-(10-2\sqrt{20}+2)\\&=(12+4\sqrt{5})-(12-4\sqrt{5})\\&=8\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored 10 worked examples covering nine distinct assessed methods, with an additional binomial example demonstrating products containing surds in both brackets. All examples use changed values and supplied booklet methods. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields; prose remains plain prose, solution ink inherits renderer blue, and bare opening expressions have phantom equals gutters. These symbolic tasks need no diagrams. Practice and quiz content were classified only and were neither altered nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual visual capture remain later stages.

examples.derivation: Distributing gives √50+√20. Removing square factors gives 5√2+2√5.
The four products give 10+3√10−2√10−6, which simplifies to 4+√10.
The four products are √50, −√30, √15 and −3. Thus the result is 5√2−√30+√15−3.
The squares are 20 and 18; the middle term is −2·2·3√10=−12√10. The result is 38−12√10.
Distribution gives 7+2√21−√84. Since √84=2√21, the surd terms cancel, leaving 7.
Expansion gives 9−12√5+20=29−12√5. Matching terms gives a=29 and b=−12.
Substitution gives 16+8√3+3−32−8√3+13. Both surd terms and the rational terms cancel, so LHS=0=RHS.
The squared binomials are 12+4√5 and 12−4√5. Subtracting the complete second expression gives 8√5.

Existing examples are correctly recorded as empty. Phantom equals gutters are appropriate; the LHS verification uses ordinary relation alignment. Fields comply with single-dollar mathematics and editable plain prose, with solution colour supplied by the confirmed renderer. These symbolic tasks require no diagrams or syllabus exceptions. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited. Actual rendered appearance remains for the later visual stage.
